hypothesis: A model choosing its own strategy can sustain and develop the same fortress past its first anniversary when cumulative execution bounds allow a long campaign.
notes: A separate condition; existing development and historical benchmark bounds/results are unchanged.
Run scripts.campaign_run for serial checkpoint-to-checkpoint continuation. Every segment owns and tears down one copied runtime before the next can start.
Max steps and the scheduling time slice are per segment. Dispatches, returned tokens and returned cost are cumulative for the campaign; continuation never resets them.
The first anniversary is 403200 elapsed ticks. It is reported, not used as an automatic success verdict or stop condition.

Twenty dollars is a returned-response cost cap, not a charge, reservation, provider billing reconciliation, or new spending authorization. Existing aggregate spending bounds still apply; a last response can cross the cap.
All models share the declared retry and grammar allowances. Native command legality remains enforced but the harness does not select a strategy or substitute WAIT.
The eight action families remain a limited interface. Starting-save digest and code/configuration identity must accompany comparisons; elapsed time alone does not prove viability.
